q145.question: What does it mean that the revealers of The Urantia Book first used "the highest human concepts" when describing God?
q145.answer:
This statement appears in the "Acknowledgment" at the very end of the Foreword. The Divine Counselor of Orvonton who wrote the Foreword, in composing these presentations about God and the universe, followed the mandate of the superuniverse rulers, which directs that in revealing truth they shall "⟦Q 0:12.11⟧give preference to the highest existing human concepts pertaining to the subjects to be presented⟦/Q⟧" [0:12.11]. Pure revelation, he says, is resorted to only when the concept of presentation has had no adequate previous expression by the human mind [0:12.11].

In other words, The Urantia Book is not a book made up solely of strange knowledge dropped from heaven; it is a book that selects and refines the best thoughts already reached by people who knew God, and that supplements them with revelation where they fall short. So there is no reason to conclude that a passage is not revelation merely because it resembles the words of the Bible or of an ancient thinker. The revealers deliberately chose such concepts.

1. Why the Foreword Was Written

The Counselor says that he was directed to write this introductory statement because there exists much confusion in the minds of Urantia mortals regarding the meanings of such terms as God, divinity, and deity [0:0.1]. The Foreword is therefore not a complete piece in itself but a guide of definitions of terms intended to help those who read the papers that follow [0:0.4]. The revealers were instructed to introduce new terms only when they could find no word in the English language that could convey the meaning even partially [0:0.2].

2. More Than a Thousand Human Concepts

The Counselor states that, in making these presentations about God and his universe associates, "⟦Q 0:12.12⟧we have selected as the basis of these papers more than one thousand human concepts⟦/Q⟧" [0:12.12]. These concepts were assembled from the God-knowing mortals of the past and the present, and where they are inadequate to portray the truth, the revealers supplement them from their own superior knowledge of the Paradise Deities and their residential universe [0:12.12]. This is not a method peculiar to this revelation alone. Successive planetary revelations of divine truth, it says, invariably embrace the highest existing concepts of spiritual values as a part of the new and enhanced co-ordination of planetary knowledge [0:12.12]. Revelation comes in a way that does not discard the best that humans have achieved but lifts it higher.

3. A Confession of the Limits of Language

The revealers do not hide the difficulty of their task. They say that it is impossible fully to translate the language of the concepts of divinity and eternity into the finite symbols of the language of the mortal mind [0:12.13]. They also say that it is exceedingly difficult to present enlarged concepts and advanced truth when they are restricted to the circumscribed language of the realm [0:0.2]. Even for words such as force, energy, and power, they confess, "⟦Q 0:6.2⟧There is such paucity of language⟦/Q⟧" [0:6.2] that they must assign multiple meanings to these terms. The Counselor of Paper 1 likewise says that he has no adequate language with which to make these universe problems clear to the mortal mind, while encouraging the reader not to be discouraged [1:7.8].

4. Why It Can Nevertheless Be Conveyed

The revealers nevertheless attempt this work because they know that a fragment of God indwells the human mind and that the Spirit of Truth sojourns with the human soul [0:12.13]. These spirit forces co-operate to enable material man to grasp the reality of spiritual values and to comprehend the philosophy of universe meanings, and they help man to make his own every truth that contributes to the enhancement of God-consciousness [0:12.13]. Paper 2 also says that without the indwelling of the Adjuster and the Spirit of Truth, all efforts to expand the concept of God would be almost futile [2:0.3]. The deeper truths about Deity will become increasingly clear as the mind is spiritualized during the ages of the ascension [1:7.8].

Summary

The revealers first used the highest concepts left by people who knew God, and supplemented them with pure revelation only where those concepts fell short [0:12.11, 0:12.12]. The Foreword is a guide to terms meant to prevent confusion [0:0.1, 0:0.4], and the revealers frankly acknowledge the limits of language [0:12.13]. What carries the writing beyond those limits and makes it living truth is the Adjuster and the Spirit of Truth within the reader [0:12.13, 2:0.3].

q146.question: What are the body, mind, spirit, soul, and personality spoken of in the Foreword, and how does the immortal soul come into being?
q146.answer:
The Foreword explains that the various properties of universe reality appear in the human experience of Urantia on the levels of body, mind, spirit, soul, and personality [0:5.6]. Put simply, body and mind are given by evolution, spirit is a gift from God, the soul is something newly born through experience, and personality is the Father's bestowal that binds all of these into one.

Of these the soul is especially important. For the soul is not there from the beginning; it is a new reality that the mind and the indwelling spirit bring forth together when a person chooses to do the will of God [0:5.10].

1. Body and Mind

The body is the material or physical organism of man, "⟦Q 0:5.7⟧Le mécanisme électrochimique vivant de nature et d’origine animales.⟦/Q⟧" [0:5.7]. Mind is the thinking, perceiving, and feeling mechanism; it is the total of conscious and unconscious experience, the intelligence associated with the emotional life, reaching upward through worship and wisdom to the spirit level [0:5.8]. But mind as it is linked with matter cannot, of itself, survive mortal death [1:3.7].

2. Spirit

Spirit here refers to the divine spirit that indwells the mind of man, that is, the Thought Adjuster [0:5.9]. This immortal spirit is destined to become a part of the surviving personality, but it is itself prepersonal, not a personality [0:5.9]. It is not yet ours by possession, but it is designed to become one with us if we survive mortal existence [1:4.3].

3. Soul

The soul is an experiential acquirement. As a mortal creature chooses to do the will of the Father in heaven, the indwelling spirit becomes the father of a new reality, and "⟦Q 0:5.10⟧Le mental mortel et matériel est la mère de cette même réalité émergente.⟦/Q⟧" [0:5.10]. This reality is neither material nor spiritual but morontial; it is the immortal soul that is destined to survive death and begin the Paradise ascension [0:5.10]. Morontia is the vast level between the material and the spiritual, whose warp is spiritual and whose woof is physical [0:5.12]. Paper 1 explains that the evolution of mind from material association to spirit association transforms the potential spirit phases of mind into the morontia reality of the immortal soul [1:3.7]. Paper 5 calls the soul "⟦Q 5:3.8⟧the conjoint creation of the God-seeking mortal mind and the God-revealing immortal Adjuster⟦/Q⟧" [5:3.8].

4. Personality

Personality is neither body, mind, spirit, nor soul. It is "⟦Q 0:5.11⟧the one changeless reality⟦/Q⟧" [0:5.11] in an otherwise ever-changing creature experience, and it unifies all other factors of individuality. Personality does not arise of itself; it is the gift of the Paradise Father [0:5.4], and it survives with the survival of the morontial soul [0:5.11]. The personality of the material self and the spirit prepersonality of the Adjuster can unite their creative attributes so as to bring into existence the surviving identity of the immortal soul [5:6.7].

5. The Growth and Survival of the Soul

The spiritual growth of the soul proceeds independently of intellectual self-consciousness [5:3.7]. So the fact that one does not feel the growth of the soul does not mean that it is absent. Survival depends on the choices of the mind: when mind believes God, soul knows God, and, with the Adjuster, they all desire God, then survival is assured [5:5.13]. Mind that yields itself to spirit becomes increasingly spiritual and attains oneness with the guiding divine spirit [1:3.7].

Summary

The body is an electrochemical mechanism, the mind is the thinking and feeling intelligence [0:5.7, 0:5.8], and the spirit is the indwelling Thought Adjuster [0:5.9]. The soul is the morontia reality that comes into being, with the Adjuster as father and the mind as mother, when one chooses the Father's will [0:5.10, 5:3.8], and personality is the Father's gift that unifies all these and survives together with the soul [0:5.11]. Choosing the Father's will day by day is the way to nurture the immortal soul [5:5.13].

q147.question: What is the "pattern" spoken of in the Foreword, and how does it differ from energy?
q147.answer:
In a word, pattern is the original from which copies are made. The Foreword defines it thus: "⟦Q 0:6.13⟧Pattern is a master design from which copies are made⟦/Q⟧" [0:6.13]. If energy is the material of reality, pattern is the form and design that this material takes. The Foreword clearly distinguishes the two by saying that pattern may configure energy but does not control it [0:6.11].

1. Energy and the Four Circuits

The Foreword first divides reality according to the circuit to which it responds. Whatever responds to the personality circuit of the Father is personal; whatever responds to the spirit circuit of the Son is spirit; whatever responds to the mind circuit of the Conjoint Actor is mind; and whatever responds to the material-gravity circuit of nether Paradise is matter [0:6.1]. Energy is an all-inclusive term applied to the spiritual, mindal, and material realms [0:6.2], and physical energy is further distinguished as space potency, primordial force, and power [0:6.4]. Mind mediates between spirit and matter in personality [0:6.8].

2. The Characteristics of Pattern

Pattern can be projected as material, spiritual, or mindal, or as any combination of these, and it can pervade personalities, identities, or nonliving matter. "⟦Q 0:6.10⟧But pattern is pattern and remains pattern; only copies are multiplied⟦/Q⟧" [0:6.10]. Pattern itself neither multiplies nor wears out; only the copies increase.

Moreover, gravity is the sole control of energy-matter, and neither space nor pattern is gravity responsive [0:6.11]. The Foreword calls pattern "⟦Q 0:6.11⟧a configuration of reality which has already paid all gravity debt⟦/Q⟧" [0:6.11], and says that the reality of any pattern consists of its energies, its mind, spirit, or material components [0:6.11].

3. The Total and the Individual

In contrast with the aspect of totality, pattern discloses the individual aspect of energy and of personality [0:6.12]. Personality or identity forms are patterns resultant from energy but are not inherent in it, and the quality of energy or of personality by virtue of which pattern is caused to appear may be attributed to God, to Deity [0:6.12]. Thus identity can be associated even with nonliving energy patterns, whereas personality is associated only with living energy systems [0:5.4].

4. The Source Patterns

The Foreword says that eternal Paradise is the absolute of patterns, the Eternal Son is the pattern personality, and the Universal Father is the direct ancestor-source of both [0:6.13]. But Paradise does not bestow pattern, and the Son cannot bestow personality [0:6.13]. The Isle of Paradise is the absolute master pattern of universe material reality [0:5.5], and the absolute personality of the Son is the divine pattern when the Father bestows personality upon the Conjoint Actor and upon countless creatures [6:7.2]. Paper 9 adds that Paradise is the pattern of infinity and the God of Action is the activator of that pattern [9:3.8]. In the local universe the Paradise Sons of the Michael order become the pattern for all personalities [1:5.6].

5. What It Means for Our Lives

The concept of pattern also helps us understand human identity. Human personality is the time-space image-shadow cast by the divine Creator personality, and the shadow must be interpreted in the light of the true substance [1:6.1]. It means that there is an original showing us what we are to grow to resemble, and the earth life of Jesus is the perfect example of that original realized within human experience [1:6.8].

Summary

Pattern, as the original from which copies are made, configures energy but does not control it; pattern itself is not multiplied, only its copies increase [0:6.10, 0:6.11, 0:6.13]. If energy tells what a thing is made of, pattern tells what form it has [0:6.11, 0:6.12]. Paradise is the pattern of matter, the Eternal Son is the pattern of personality, and the Father is the source of both [0:6.13, 0:5.5].

q148.question: What does the command "Be you perfect, even as I am perfect" mean for finite human beings?
q148.answer:
These words are the "supreme mandate" [1:0.3] that has gone forth from the Universal Father who inhabits eternity. The Urantia Book does not take this command to mean that human beings must become as perfect as the infinite God. It says that Urantia mortals can hardly hope to be perfect in the infinite sense, but that it is entirely possible for them, starting out on this planet, to attain the divine goal that God has set [1:0.5]. It is, in other words, a call for each to attain divine perfection in his own sphere.

1. The Source and Transmission of the Command

In love and mercy the messengers of Paradise have carried this divine exhortation down through the ages and out through the universes, even to such lowly animal-origin creatures as the human races of Urantia [1:0.3]. The Eternal Son, too, without reservation joined the Father in broadcasting this mandate to all creation [7:5.1], and the Father entrusted the execution of this vast undertaking to the Eternal Son [7:4.7]. Ever since, this mandate has motivated all the survival plans and bestowal plans carried out by the Sons of God [7:5.1].

2. What Kind of Perfection

The perfection that human beings attain may not be universal in the material sense, unlimited in intellectual grasp, or final in spiritual experience. But "⟦Q 1:0.5⟧it is final and complete in all finite aspects of divinity of will, perfection of personality motivation, and God-consciousness⟦/Q⟧" [1:0.5]. In other words, it is to become perfect in what one wills, in why one acts, and in how fully one is conscious of God. Then a person becomes just as replete in his sphere as God is in his [1:0.5].

3. The First Duty and the Certain Destiny

This exhortation to strive for the perfection of divinity is the first duty, and should be the highest ambition, of every struggling creature [1:0.4]. At the same time, the possibility of attaining divine perfection is the final and certain destiny of man's eternal spiritual progress [1:0.4]. This command always moves a person forward, calling him into the long and fascinating struggle toward higher spiritual values [1:0.6].

4. Perfection Gained Through Experience

The beings of Havona are what they are by virtue of existing, but mortal man earns even his status as an ascension candidate by his own faith and hope [3:5.16]. Everything divine that the human mind grasps and the soul acquires is an experiential attainment [3:5.16]. The creature mind must attain divine perfection through the experiential transformations of spiritual attainment that result from choosing to do the will of the Father in heaven [1:3.6]. The whole plan of the space worlds is centered on the divine purpose of elevating every will creature to the experience of sharing the Father's Paradise perfection [2:2.5].

5. How It Is Accomplished

This is not something one does by one's own strength alone. The Father's plan of progressive attainment includes the bestowal of the Thought Adjuster and the prerogatives of personality [7:4.4]. If a person, with spiritual motivation, devotes himself wholeheartedly to doing the Father's will, the consciousness of knowing God and the experience of becoming more and more like him will surely be realized [5:1.6]. If one yields to the leading of the indwelling spirit, he will be led step by step, unerringly, until at last he stands in the Father's presence [2:5.5]. On that way a person must be spiritually transformed many times before he attains the spiritual vision to see even one of the Seven Master Spirits [5:1.1], but that way is open to all of us [5:1.8].

Summary

This command does not demand infinite perfection; it is a call to attain, in will, motive, and God-consciousness, the perfection proper to each one's sphere [1:0.5]. It is the first duty and the certain destiny [1:0.4], something gained one step at a time through experience [3:5.16], and accomplished with the help of the Adjuster and the divine Sons [7:4.4, 7:4.7].

q149.question: If the existence of God cannot be proved by science or logic, how can a person be sure that God exists?
q149.answer:
The Urantia Book says plainly, "⟦Q 1:2.7⟧The existence of God can never be proved by scientific experiment or by the pure reason of logical deduction⟦/Q⟧" [1:2.7]. God can be realized only in the realms of human experience [1:2.7]. But this does not mean that certainty about God is impossible; it means that this certainty comes not from a proof of the head but from living experience. And the ground of that experience is the spirit of God who actually dwells within us.

1. Three Signs Given by the Indwelling Adjuster

The fact of the existence of God is demonstrated in human experience through the divine presence that lives in the mind of mortal man, the Adjuster [1:2.3]. This presence can be known through three experiential phenomena. The first is the intellectual capacity for knowing God, God-consciousness [1:2.4]; the second is the spiritual urge to find God, God-seeking [1:2.5]; and the third is the personality craving to be like God, to do the will of the Father [1:2.6]. The very desire to seek God is in itself a sign that he exists. Paper 2 also says that the greatest evidence of the goodness of God is this indwelling Adjuster [2:5.5].

2. Experience as the Only Positive Proof

"⟦Q 1:2.8⟧Those who know God have experienced the fact of his presence⟦/Q⟧" [1:2.8]. God-knowing mortals hold in their personal experience the only positive proof of the existence of the living God which one human being can offer to another [1:2.8]. The existence of God is utterly beyond all possibility of demonstration except for the contact between the God-consciousness of the human mind and the God-presence of the indwelling Adjuster [1:2.8]. In the spiritual experience of man God is a reality, not a mystery; the mystery arises when one attempts to explain the realities of spirit to the material mind [1:4.7].

3. The Place of Reason and Revelation

This does not mean that reason is useless. To science God is a cause, to philosophy an idea, to religion a person, even the loving heavenly Father [1:6.2]. The true concept of God is reasonable to logic, plausible to philosophy, and essential to religion [1:2.7]. Reason, wisdom, and religious experience infer and imply the personality of God, but they do not altogether validate it [1:5.10]. That the First Cause of science and the self-existent Unity of philosophy is the God who is full of mercy and goodness can be known only through revelation [4:4.7]. Ultimate universe reality cannot be grasped by mathematics, logic, or philosophy, but only by personal experience in progressive conformity to the will of God [1:7.5].

4. Fruits Rather Than Feelings

The failure to be intellectually conscious of contact with the indwelling Adjuster does not in any way disprove that experience [5:2.4]. The proof of fraternity with the divine Adjuster consists in the nature and extent of the fruits of the spirit that are yielded in the life of the believer [5:2.4]. Certainty therefore shows itself more clearly in the transformation of life than in special emotions [5:2.6].

5. The Attitude of Sharing One's Certainty

One may argue opinions about God, but experience with God transcends all controversy. The God-knowing person describes his experiences not to convince unbelievers but for the edification of believers [1:6.6]. For the concept of a divine personality can be grasped only by the spiritual insight of genuine personal religious experience [1:6.4].

Summary

The existence of God is not proved by experiment or logic, but it is made certain in experience through the presence of the indwelling spirit, which reveals itself in God-consciousness, God-seeking, and the craving to be like God [1:2.3-2.6, 1:2.8]. Reason shows that this certainty is reasonable, and revelation makes known that this God is the loving Father [1:2.7, 4:4.7], while the proof of that certainty is the fruit of the spirit borne in one's life [5:2.4].

q150.question: Why is the infinite God called a "personality," and why does that matter for our life of faith?
q150.answer:
The Urantia Book affirms that God is at once infinite and personal: "⟦Q 1:5.1⟧God is both infinite and personal; he is an infinite personality⟦/Q⟧" [1:5.1]. God far transcends the human concept of personality, but that does not mean he could be anything less than a personality; he cannot be anything less than an eternal, infinite, true, good, and beautiful personality [1:5.2]. This truth matters because it is only with a God who is a personality that we can share love and fellowship.

1. Beyond Personality, but Never Less Than Personality

God is an eternal power, a majestic presence, a transcendent ideal, and a glorious spirit, yet while he is all these, he is truly a perfect Creator personality [1:5.8]. Personality is not one of the many attributes of God; it signifies the totality of his co-ordinated infinite nature and unified divine will, and in the supreme sense it is the revelation of God to the universe of universes [1:5.13]. Without God there would be no personality anywhere in the universe [1:5.7].

2. Personality Without a Body

We must abandon the idea that the concept of personality must carry with it a material form [1:5.12]. Because of this error of corporeality, materialism holds that personality ends when a man dies, and pantheism holds that God is not a person because he has no body [1:5.12]. If the personality of the First Source and Center is denied, only these two philosophic dilemmas remain [1:5.11]. The concept of the personality of God is a truer concept that has come to mankind chiefly through revelation, and the maturity of any religion is in direct proportion to its grasp of the concept of the infinite personality of God [1:5.10].

3. Fellowship Becomes Possible

The concept of the personality of Deity facilitates fellowship, favors intelligent worship, and promotes refreshing trustfulness [1:7.1]. "⟦Q 1:7.1⟧Entre choses non personnelles il peut y avoir interaction, mais non communion.⟦/Q⟧" [1:7.1]. Man does not become one with God as a drop of water merges into the ocean; he attains divine union through personal communion with the personal God and wholehearted conformity to the divine will [1:7.2]. We do not dissolve and disappear in God; we fellowship with him and grow more and more like him. The concept of a divine personality can be grasped only by the spiritual insight of genuine personal religious experience [1:6.4], and the more deeply a person recognizes the personality value of himself and his fellows, the more he longs to know the Original Personality [1:6.6].

4. Goodness and Love Only in Personality

The concepts of truth and beauty can be entertained without personality, but divine goodness is understood only in relation to personality. Only a personality can love and be loved [1:7.3]. Man may fear a great God, but he trusts and loves only a good God [2:6.1].

5. God Who Becomes Our Friend

God can become our friend, and "⟦Q 1:5.8⟧you can be known, as other humans have been known, as the friend of God⟦/Q⟧" [1:5.8]. But because friendship between two personalities requires moral affinity and spiritual harmony, to know a divine personality all the personality endowments of man must be wholly consecrated to the effort; half-hearted devotion is unavailing [1:6.5]. Even though material mortals cannot see the personality of God, they should rejoice in the assurance that he is a person [1:5.4]. The Father who is a person participates directly in the struggles of every imperfect soul seeking to ascend; he suffers with us in all our afflictions and triumphs with us in our victories [1:5.15, 1:5.16].

Summary

God is infinite and yet a true personality; he transcends the human concept of personality but is never less than a personality [1:5.1, 1:5.2]. Only with a God who is a personality are fellowship, worship, and trust possible [1:7.1, 1:7.2]; only so do goodness and love have meaning [1:7.3], and only so can we become his friends [1:5.8].

q151.question: Do God's justice and mercy not clash with each other, and how does The Urantia Book explain the two?
q151.answer:
The answer of The Urantia Book is clear: in God justice and mercy do not clash. The heavenly Father is never torn by conflicting attitudes towards his children; "⟦Q 2:4.3⟧Dieu n’est jamais victime d’antagonismes dans sa manière de voir.⟦/Q⟧" [2:4.3]. Mercy is not a violation of justice; it is justice applied with infinite wisdom in consideration of the situation of finite creatures.

Many theologies have pictured God as one in conflict, torn between a judge who demands justice and a father who wishes to forgive. The Urantia Book corrects this picture. The affectionate heavenly Father is not a divided personality, one of justice and one of mercy [2:6.6].

1. The Justice of God

God is righteous; therefore he is fair. The justice of the Universal Father is not influenced by the acts or performances of his creatures, and God is no respecter of persons [2:3.1]. A man reaps what he sows, and it is futile to make puerile appeals to God in order to avoid the just consequences of natural laws and spiritual mandates [2:3.2]. Yet even in the justice of reaping the harvest of wrongdoing, divine justice is always tempered with mercy [2:3.2].

2. What Mercy Is

The Urantia Book defines mercy thus: "⟦Q 2:4.1⟧Mercy is simply justice tempered by that wisdom which grows out of perfection of knowledge and the full recognition of the natural weaknesses and environmental handicaps of finite creatures⟦/Q⟧" [2:4.1]. Mercy is not a contravention of justice but the justice of supremacy adjusted to the situations of the evolving finite, an understanding interpretation of the demands of supreme justice [2:4.5]. Mercy is the natural and inevitable offspring of goodness and love [2:4.4].

3. Wisdom Determines the Proportions

Infinite wisdom is the eternal arbiter which determines the proportions of justice and mercy to be meted out in any given circumstance [2:3.2]. Only the discernment of infinite wisdom enables a righteous God to minister justice and mercy at the same time, and God's all-knowingness directs his free will in choosing conduct that perfectly, simultaneously, and equally satisfies the demands of all his attributes [2:4.3]. Eternal justice and divine mercy together constitute what in human experience would be called fairness [2:4.4].

4. The Father's Mercy Need Not Be Drawn Out

God is inherently kind and eternally merciful, and no influence ever needs to be exerted upon the Father to call forth his loving-kindness [2:4.2]. The creature's need is wholly sufficient to insure the full flow of the Father's mercy, and because God knows all about his children, it is easy for him to forgive [2:4.2]. Therefore the Father does not require a mediator to secure his favor or forgiveness, and "⟦Q 2:6.6⟧God as a father transcends God as a judge⟦/Q⟧" [2:6.6]. Of course his wisdom at times restrains his love, and justice conditions rejected mercy [2:6.7].

5. Where Justice and Mercy Become One

The Urantia Book explains justice as the collective thought of righteousness and mercy as its personal expression [10:6.18]. When fully perceived and completely understood, the righteous justice of the Trinity and the merciful love of the Universal Father coincide [10:6.18]. It is only because man does not so fully understand divine justice that the two appear to be separate [10:6.18]. Just as the more deeply we understand our neighbor, the easier it becomes to forgive him [2:4.2], so the deeper our understanding becomes, the better we see the oneness of justice and mercy.

Summary

God's justice is fair and impartial but is always tempered with mercy [2:3.1, 2:3.2], and mercy is not a violation of justice but justice tempered by wisdom and interpreted to fit the finite situation [2:4.1, 2:4.5]. Because infinite wisdom satisfies both at the same time, God is never a divided personality [2:4.3, 2:6.6], and when fully understood, the justice of the Trinity and the love of the Father coincide [10:6.18].

q152.question: What does it mean that "God loves not like a father, but as a father"?
q152.answer:
This sentence appears in Paper 2, section 6: "⟦Q 2:6.4⟧God loves not like a father, but as a father⟦/Q⟧" [2:6.4]. "Like a father" is a simile; it says that God's love resembles a father's love. But "as a father" is not a figure of speech; it speaks of an actual relationship. God really is our Father, for he is the Paradise Father of every universe personality [2:6.4].

1. From King and Judge to Father

The concept of God as a king-judge fostered a high moral standard and created a law-respecting people, but it left the individual believer in a position of insecurity respecting his status in time and in eternity [2:6.4]. The later Hebrew prophets proclaimed God to be a Father to Israel, and Jesus revealed God as the Father of each human being [2:6.4]. Jesus lifted the old concept of a God dominated by the morality of kings up to the intimate family morality of the parent-child relationship [2:6.2]. Selflessness is inherent in parental love [2:6.4].

2. The Character of the Father's Love

"God is love"; therefore his only personal attitude towards the affairs of the universe is always a reaction of divine affection [2:5.1]. But that love is not a sentimental love; it is an intelligent and farseeing parental affection, functioning in unified association with divine wisdom and all his other infinite characteristics [2:5.10]. That is why The Urantia Book adds, "⟦Q 2:5.10⟧God is love, but love is not God⟦/Q⟧" [2:5.10]. Because God's love is by nature a fatherly affection, he sometimes chastens us for our own good, and he suffers with us even in our fiery trials [2:5.3].

3. A Love That No One Had to Win

It is a mistake to think that God was led to love his children because of the sacrifices of his Sons or the intercession of his subordinate creatures [2:5.2]. The Father himself loves us, and it is in response to this very affection that he sends the Adjusters into the minds of men [2:5.2]. The Father's love is universal, and he is not willing that any should perish [2:5.2].

4. The Greatest Proof of Love

The greatest manifestation of the divine love for mortal beings is observed in the bestowal of the Thought Adjusters, and the greatest revelation of the Father's love is seen in the bestowal life of Michael, who lived on earth the ideal spiritual life [2:5.10]. It is the indwelling Adjuster who individualizes the love of God to each human soul [2:5.10]. The greatest evidence of the goodness of God and the supreme reason for loving him is that indwelling gift, which patiently awaits the hour when it will be eternally one with us [2:5.5].

5. Our Response as Children

"⟦Q 2:5.8⟧L’expérience d’aimer est dans une grande mesure une réponse directe à l’expérience d’être aimé.⟦/Q⟧" [2:5.8]. When we contemplate the loving nature of God, there is only one reasonable and natural response: to love the Maker more and more [2:5.9]. The love of the infinite Father can actually be experienced by finite man, and the measure of that experience is determined by our spiritual capacity of receptivity and our ability to love the Father in return [3:4.6]. Therefore man's nearest approach to God is by and through love [3:4.7].

Summary

God is not one who resembles a father; he actually is the Father of all personalities, and his love is not a figure of speech but an actual relationship [2:6.4]. That love is a wise and farseeing parental affection [2:5.10]; it was not won through anyone's intercession [2:5.2], and it has been most fully shown in the indwelling of the Adjuster and in the life of Michael [2:5.10]. Our response is to receive that love and to love all the more [2:5.8, 2:5.9].

q153.question: It is said that God loves the sinner and hates the sin; what becomes of a being who chooses sin to the very end?
q153.answer:
According to The Urantia Book, a being who identifies himself with sin to the very end does not undergo eternal torture; his existence is ended. "⟦Q 2:3.2⟧The final result of wholehearted sin is annihilation⟦/Q⟧" [2:3.2]. Yet this annihilation is not so much God's retribution as self-destruction: by embracing to the end that which is not real, the being himself becomes unreal [2:3.2]. And that verdict is pronounced only after mercy has done everything it can.

1. God Who Distinguishes the Sinner from the Sin

Persons can love and hate only other persons, and sin is not a person [2:6.8]. God loves the sinner because he is a personality reality, potentially eternal, but towards sin God strikes no personal attitude; only the justice of God takes cognizance of its existence [2:6.8]. "⟦Q 2:6.8⟧The love of God saves the sinner; the law of God destroys the sin⟦/Q⟧" [2:6.8]. His love of righteousness cannot but be shown as an equal hatred of sin [2:6.7].

2. Annihilation Is an Inevitable Consequence

The greatest punishment for deliberate rebellion is in reality an inevitable consequence: loss of existence as an individual subject of the government of God [2:3.2]. Sin-identified individuals have destroyed themselves by becoming wholly unreal through their embrace of iniquity [2:3.2]. Undiluted evil and deliberate sin are inherently and automatically suicidal [2:3.5]. Unreality cannot exist forever in a progressingly real and increasingly spiritual universe [2:6.8].

3. A Delayed Verdict

The factual disappearance of such a creature is always delayed until the ordained order of justice current in that universe has been fully complied with [2:3.2]. Extinction is usually decreed at the dispensational adjudication, and it may be decreed by the co-ordinate action of all the tribunals of jurisdiction, from the planetary council through the courts of the Creator Son up to the tribunals of the Ancients of Days [2:3.3]. The Creator Sons of the local universes devote themselves to rehabilitating the rebellious and the wrong-thinking, and only when all their loving efforts are finally and forever spurned is the decree of extinction executed [2:3.6]. Meanwhile the attitude of unreality survives in the universe because of the transient tolerance of mercy [2:3.5].

4. After Annihilation

When the sentence is confirmed, the sin-identified being instantly becomes as though he had not been. "⟦Q 2:3.4⟧There is no resurrection from such a fate⟦/Q⟧" [2:3.4]. The living energy factors of identity are resolved into cosmic potentials, and the isolated personality is absorbed into the oversoul of creation, becoming a part of the evolving experience of the Supreme Being [2:3.4]. In the case of an Adjuster-indwelt personality, the experiential spirit values survive in the reality of the continuing Adjuster [2:3.4].

5. The Door of Choice Is Open

This teaching is not meant to instill fear. Man's final destiny is not settled until he has lost the power to choose the Father's will, and the Father's heart is never closed to the need and petition of his children [5:1.11]. Moreover, erroneous judgment, the possibility of evil, becomes sin only when the human will consciously endorses a deliberate immoral judgment [3:5.15]. It is not that God desires the annihilation of the sinner; it is the choice to reject life to the very end that causes life to be lost [2:3.4].

Summary

God loves the sinner and deals with sin by justice [2:6.8], and a being who identifies himself with sin to the very end comes to annihilation without resurrection [2:3.2, 2:3.4]. It is not retribution but the self-destruction of one who chose unreality [2:3.5], and it is pronounced only after every effort at rehabilitation and every procedure of justice has been exhausted [2:3.3, 2:3.6]. As long as the power of choice remains, the way back to the Father is always open [5:1.11].

q154.question: How are truth, beauty, and goodness related, and why does religion today need all three together?
q154.answer:
The Urantia Book regards truth, beauty, and goodness not as separate values but as divine realities woven into one. "⟦Q 2:7.12⟧La vérité est cohérente, la beauté est attrayante, la bonté est stabilisante.⟦/Q⟧" [2:7.12]. When these three are co-ordinated in personality experience, the result is a high order of love conditioned by wisdom and qualified by loyalty [2:7.12]. And it diagnoses one of the reasons why religion today fails to hold people's hearts as its emphasis on goodness alone, isolated from the other two [2:7.9].

1. Where the Three Are Revealed

In the physical universe we see the divine beauty, in the intellectual world we discern eternal truth, but the goodness of God is found only in the spiritual world of personal religious experience [2:6.1]. The concepts of truth and beauty can be entertained without personality, but divine goodness is understood only in relation to personality [1:7.3]. Even beauty and truth would be divorced from the hope of survival were they not attributes of a loving Father [1:7.3].

2. Truth

Physical facts are fairly uniform, but truth is a living and flexible factor in the philosophy of the universe [2:7.2]. "⟦Q 2:7.4⟧La vérité est belle parce qu’elle est à la fois complète et symétrique.⟦/Q⟧" [2:7.4]. Because truth can be acted upon and lived, happiness follows its recognition, and divine truth is best recognized by its spiritual flavor [2:7.6]. Conversely, the error of abstraction, which grasps one aspect of reality and pronounces it the whole truth, is the philosopher's gravest error [2:7.5].

3. Beauty

The discernment of supreme beauty is the discovery and integration of reality [2:7.8]. "⟦Q 2:7.8⟧Discerner la bonté divine dans la vérité éternelle, c’est la beauté ultime.⟦/Q⟧" [2:7.8]. Even the charm of human art consists in the harmony of its unity [2:7.8]. Beauty, we might say, is the way we recognize truth and goodness harmonized into one.

4. A Diagnosis of the Hebrew Religion and of Modern Religion

The great mistake of the Hebrew religion was its failure to associate the goodness of God with the factual truths of science and the beauty of art [2:7.9]. As religion overemphasized goodness while relatively excluding truth and neglecting beauty, certain types of men increasingly turned away from the abstract concept of isolated goodness [2:7.9]. The isolated morality of modern religion will recover itself when it gives equal consideration to the truths of science, philosophy, and spiritual experience, to the beauties of the physical creation and the charm of art, and to the grandeur of genuine character achievement [2:7.9]. The religious challenge of this age is to build a new and appealing philosophy of living from the unified concepts of truth, beauty, and goodness [2:7.10].

5. The Fruits of Unification

All truth is beautiful and good; all real beauty is true and good; all genuine goodness is true and beautiful [2:7.11]. Health, sanity, and happiness are integrations of truth, beauty, and goodness as they are blended in human experience [2:7.11]. As man ascends the steps of the spiritual life, these three become increasingly co-ordinated and unified in the God who is love [2:7.10]. The God of love revealed by Jesus embraces truth, beauty, and goodness alike [5:4.6].

Summary

Truth coheres, beauty attracts, and goodness stabilizes, and when the three are harmonized they become a high order of love [2:7.12]. Goodness is understood in personal relationship [1:7.3], truth is beautiful because it is symmetrical [2:7.4], and discerning goodness within truth is ultimate beauty [2:7.8]. A religion that isolates goodness loses its power, so religion today must unite the three once again [2:7.9, 2:7.10].

q155.question: If God knows all things, how can human free will be true freedom?
q155.answer:
The Urantia Book teaches that God's omniscience and human freedom do not cancel each other out. "⟦Q 3:3.4⟧Mais, même si Dieu connaissait d’avance les actes de libre arbitre de ses enfants, sa prescience n’abrogerait nullement leur liberté.⟦/Q⟧" [3:3.4]. To know is not the same as to determine. God knows all things, but he has left to man the choice concerning his eternal destiny.

1. God's Knowledge Is Universal

God knows all things, and his knowledge of events is universal and perfect [3:3.1]. Not a sparrow falls to the ground without the Father's knowledge, and even the hairs of our head are numbered [3:3.1]. His personality circuit embraces all personalities, and his knowledge is supplemented through the divine Sons and the indwelling Thought Adjusters [3:3.3]. With God there is no past, present, or future; all time is present to him [2:1.5]. He knows what we need even before we ask him [3:3.2].

2. Knowing Is Not Determining

The Urantia Book speaks carefully. It cannot say for certain whether or not God chooses to foreknow events of sin, but even if he should foreknow them, that knowledge does not abrogate freedom, and one thing is certain: God is never subjected to surprise [3:3.4]. And just as omnipotence does not imply the power to do the ungodlike act, "⟦Q 3:3.5⟧L’omniscience n’implique pas non plus la connaissance de ce qui est inconnaissable.⟦/Q⟧" [3:3.5]. It adds that it is almost impossible for the finite mind fully to comprehend this matter [3:3.5].

3. The Sovereignty of the Will Guaranteed by God

Having bestowed personality, the Father stands aside, and it remains for man himself to will the creation or to inhibit the creation of the surviving and eternal self [5:6.8]. No being in the universe can interfere with the sovereignty of the mortal free will regarding eternal destiny. "⟦Q 5:6.8⟧Quant à la survie éternelle, Dieu a décrété que la volonté matérielle et humaine était souveraine, et ce décret est absolu.⟦/Q⟧" [5:6.8]. No personal creature can be forced into the eternal adventure; the portals of eternity open only in response to the freewill choice [5:6.12]. The Creator refuses to coerce or compel the submission of the spiritual free wills of his material creatures [1:1.2].

4. Freedom and the Plan Go Together

In the things that take place within a man's heart, the Father's will may not always be done, but in the course and destiny of a planet the divine plan prevails [3:5.3]. The Father knows the end from the beginning, and his divine plan actually embraces and encompasses all the experiments and adventures carried out by all his subordinates [2:1.4]. Evolving man must be fallible if he is to be free, and free and inexperienced intelligence cannot at first be uniformly wise [3:5.15]. The Father generally rules through his Sons and their subordinates, and he usually exercises delegated power directly only when the personalities to whom it was delegated have failed in their trust [3:5.1].

5. What It Means for Us

The extent to which the Father's presence works within us is determined not by any whim of God but by our own choices [3:1.12]. Man's final destiny is not settled until he has lost the power to choose the Father's will [5:1.11]. The fact that God knows all things is not a fatalism that binds us; it is a comfort, for whatever we choose, he is never taken aback and he cares for us to the end [3:3.2].

Summary

God knows all things and is never surprised, but that knowledge does not in the least abrogate the freedom of his children [3:3.1, 3:3.4]. The sovereignty of the human will regarding eternal survival is an absolute decree established by God himself [5:6.8], and the divine plan embraces even the adventure of that freedom [2:1.4, 3:5.3]. Our choices are therefore real choices [5:6.12].

q156.question: Why are the uncertainties and hardships of life necessary, and how do they make human beings different from the perfect beings of Havona?
q156.answer:
The Urantia Book says that the uncertainties of life and the vicissitudes of existence in no way contradict the universal sovereignty of God [3:5.5]. On the contrary, the most precious virtues, such as courage, altruism, hope, and faith, cannot come into being without an environment that tests and develops them. That is why the life of every evolving creature is beset by certain inevitabilities [3:5.5].

1. Virtues Paired with Environments

Paper 3 explains this principle through nine questions. If courage is desirable, man must grow up in an environment that necessitates grappling with hardships and reacting to disappointments [3:5.6]. If altruism is desirable, he must come face to face with situations of social inequality [3:5.7]. If hope is desirable, he must meet constant insecurity and recurrent uncertainties [3:5.8]. If faith is desirable, "⟦Q 3:5.9⟧Alors, il faut que le mental de l’homme se retrouve dans cette situation embarrassante où il en sait toujours moins que ce qu’il peut croire.⟦/Q⟧" [3:5.9]. To love truth, he must grow up in a world where error is present [3:5.10]; if loyalty is desirable, he must carry on amid the possibilities of betrayal and desertion [3:5.12]. Even the satisfaction of happiness can be enjoyed only in a world where the alternative of pain is always open [3:5.14].

2. A Self to Deny and the Contrast of Evil

If unselfishness is desirable, man must live face to face with the incessant clamoring of the self for recognition and honor [3:5.13]. Without a self life to deny, he could not dynamically choose the divine life, and without potential evil to distinguish good by contrast, he could not lay saving hold on righteousness [3:5.13]. For all the phases of relative good to be revealed, there must always be the contrast of comparative evil, though not of sin [4:3.6].

3. Freedom Brings the Possibility of Error

The only evolutionary world without error would be a world without free intelligence. "⟦Q 3:5.15⟧Evolving man must be fallible if he is to be free⟦/Q⟧" [3:5.15]. Yet the possibility of mistaken judgment becomes sin only when the human will consciously endorses a deliberate immoral judgment [3:5.15].

4. The Difference Between Havona Beings and Human Beings

The perfect beings of Havona discern and choose the good without contrasting moral situations; they are what they are by virtue of existing [3:5.16]. They are courageous by nature, but not with courage in the human sense; they are kind, but hardly altruistic in the human way; they expect a pleasant future, but do not hope in the manner of the trusting mortal of an uncertain world [3:5.17]. They do not know the saving faith that lifts mortal man from the status of an animal up to the portals of Paradise [3:5.17]. By contrast, everything divine that man gains is an experiential attainment, a unique possession in contrast with the innate goodness of the Havona personalities [3:5.16].

5. The Attitude of Faith Toward Suffering

Because we are members of God's family, we must sometimes share in the family discipline [3:2.9]. Because of the limits of our vision, many divine acts may appear harsh, yet all of God's acts are purposeful and wise and take into account the highest good of all concerned [3:2.8]. "⟦Q 9:1.8⟧The universe of your origin is being forged out between the anvil of justice and the hammer of suffering⟦/Q⟧" [9:1.8]. But those who wield the hammer are the children of the Infinite Spirit, the children of mercy [9:1.8].

Summary

Virtues such as courage, altruism, hope, faith, and loyalty grow only amid the hardships and uncertainties that pair with them [3:5.6-5.14], and freedom carries with it the possibility of error [3:5.15]. Havona beings are good by nature, but human beings gain goodness through experience, and that is the unique treasure of mortals [3:5.16, 3:5.17]. The hand that deals with suffering is the hand of mercy [9:1.8].

q157.question: If God does not change, how can he have free will and form a living relationship with his creatures?
q157.answer:
The Urantia Book warns us not to understand God's changelessness as "not moving." God can modify the manifestations of his absoluteness, passing from simplicity to complexity, from quiescence to motion, from infinity to finitude, "⟦Q 4:4.2⟧because divine immutability does not imply immobility⟦/Q⟧" [4:4.2]. And it immediately adds, "⟦Q 4:4.2⟧God has will—he is will⟦/Q⟧" [4:4.2]. What does not change is his character and purpose; the will that flows from that character responds to us in a living and free way.

1. What Does Not Change

God is the only stationary, self-contained, and changeless being in the whole universe of universes, having no outside, no beyond, no past, and no future [4:4.1]. Because he is self-existent he is absolutely independent, and his very identity is inimical to change [4:4.2]. The olden prophets also knew this in the words, "⟦Q 2:2.1⟧I am the Lord; I change not⟦/Q⟧" [2:2.1]. Thus the plans and purposes of the First Source and Center are like himself: eternal, perfect, and changeless [2:2.1]. God never regrets what he has done or will do, because his foreknowledge guides his creative free will [4:3.4].

2. Why Then Does He Seem to Change?

In the execution of his eternal purpose, the reactions of the changeless God may seem to vary in accordance with the changing attitudes and shifting minds of intelligent beings; "⟦Q 2:2.3⟧they may apparently and superficially vary⟦/Q⟧" [2:2.3], but underneath there is always the changeless purpose and the everlasting plan [2:2.3]. The Father never makes mistakes and never repents, yet his heart is no doubt saddened when his children fail to attain the spiritual levels they are capable of reaching [4:3.5]. It is because an unchanging love deals with changing children that its responses appear so varied.

3. Absolute Self-Determination and Infinite Will

God is a being of absolute self-determination; there are no limits to his universe reactions save those which are self-imposed, and his freewill acts are conditioned only by the divine qualities of his eternal nature [4:4.3]. Personality and goodness he shares with man, but infinity of will is his alone [4:4.4]. Moreover, to deny him the possibility of volitional self-limitation would amount to denying the concept of his volitional absoluteness [4:4.4]. That God limits his presence is likewise because such is his will [3:2.15].

4. A Father Who Rules by Emotion

The absoluteness of God pervades all seven levels of universe reality, but the whole of that absolute nature is subject to the relationship of the Creator to his creature family [4:4.5]. The justice of the Trinity is precise, but in his family relationship with the creatures of time the God of universes is governed by divine sentiment [4:4.5]. In the Father freewill performances are not ruled by power, nor are they guided by intellect alone; the divine personality manifests himself as love [4:4.6]. "⟦Q 4:4.6⟧God is a Father in the highest sense of the term⟦/Q⟧" [4:4.6].

5. The Changeless God in a Changing Universe

We cannot fully understand how God can be changeless and yet be surrounded by an ever-changing evolutionary universe, but we can know that truth through experience, for we ourselves maintain identity of personality and unity of will amid a changing environment [1:7.4]. God does not grow in knowledge, but he enjoys a continuing expansion of self-realization within his personality realm [1:5.14], and he participates directly in the struggles of every soul seeking to ascend [1:5.15]. That is why the believer, facing his limitations, can declare: "⟦Q 4:4.9⟧Even if I cannot do this, there lives in me one who can and will do it⟦/Q⟧" [4:4.9].

Summary

God's character and purpose are eternally changeless [2:2.1, 4:4.2], but changelessness is not immobility, and God is infinite will [4:4.2, 4:4.4]. His reactions seem to change according to the attitudes of his children, but beneath them lies the unchanging plan [2:2.3], and in his relationship with his creatures he rules by divine sentiment, the heart of a loving Father [4:4.5, 4:4.6]. Thus the God who does not change is the most trustworthy and living Father.

q158.question: How do the Eternal Son of Paradise and Michael (Jesus), who came to this earth, differ, and why are the two often confused?
q158.answer:
The Eternal Son is the original and only-begotten Son of God, the second person of Deity, the Second Source and Center [6:1.1]. Michael is one of the Creator Sons personalized jointly by the Universal Father and the Eternal Son; he made and rules the local universe of Nebadon and was incarnated on this earth as Jesus of Nazareth [7:6.3, 1:2.9]. Michael, therefore, is not the Eternal Son himself but a son of the Eternal Son. The Urantia Book points out that on our world the Eternal Son "⟦Q 6:1.5⟧has been confused with a co-ordinate Creator Son, Michael of Nebadon⟦/Q⟧" [6:1.5].

1. Who the Eternal Son Is

The Eternal Son is the perfect and final expression of the first personal and absolute concept of the Universal Father; he is the living divine Word, who always was and forever is [6:0.1]. "⟦Q 6:2.2⟧Le Fils Éternel est le Verbe éternel de Dieu.⟦/Q⟧" [6:2.2]. If the Father is first a creator and then a controller, the Eternal Son is first a cocreator and then a spiritual administrator [6:1.2]. He is omnipotent only in the spiritual realm [6:4.2], and because he is an infinite and exclusively personal being, he cannot fragmentize and bestow himself [6:5.5]. That is why it is customary to apply the title Eternal Son only to this Original Son [6:1.6].

2. Who Michael Is

Whenever the Father and the Eternal Son jointly project a new and absolute personal thought, that idea is personalized in the person of a new Creator Son [7:6.3]. The Creator Sons go out from Paradise into the universes of time and complete the organization of the local universes [7:6.4], and we and our universe were created by a Creator Son of the Eternal Son and a Creative Spirit of the Infinite Spirit [8:3.4]. A Creator Son represents both the Father and the Son to the creatures of ten million inhabited worlds [6:8.3].

3. Why They Are Confused

The Urantia Book says that the words of the Gospel of John, "⟦Q 6:1.3⟧In the beginning was the Word⟦/Q⟧," would have been true had they referred to the Eternal Son [6:1.3]. Those who associated with Jesus also called him the Word of life, and a bestowal Son came forth from the Father just as truly as did the Original Son [6:1.4]. Above all, the Eternal Son cannot himself become flesh, yet when the divine person of Michael was incarnated in the human nature of Jesus of Nazareth, the Eternal Son actually came to the mortals of Urantia [7:5.4]. In the bestowal of each Son of God it becomes true that the Eternal Son has bestowed himself in that bestowal [7:5.10], and "⟦Q 7:5.11⟧Il est littéralement vrai que quiconque a vu un Fils du Paradis a vu le Fils Éternel de Dieu.⟦/Q⟧" [7:5.11]. Because the two are thus as one in spirit and nature, they are easily mixed up.

4. The Differences That Must Still Be Kept

The nature of a Creator Son does not embrace all the unqualified potentialities of the First Source and Center, yet the Universal Father is in every way present in him [1:5.6]. The Creator Sons are not concerned with the central control of matter, mind, and spirit, and they can administer only what they themselves have brought into being [7:6.4]. The Eternal Son transmits creatorship only to his first personalization, and a Creator Son cannot further transmit that prerogative [6:5.4]. Just as the Eternal Son and the Creator Sons must be distinguished, so must the Infinite Spirit and the Creative Spirits of the local universes be distinguished [9:8.5].

5. In Our Experience

In the local universe ascension we recognize the Creator Son as the personal representative of the Eternal Son [7:3.1], and the understandable personality of the Creator Son compensates for our inability to grasp the more spiritual Eternal Son [6:8.7]. Only when we are spiritualized and begin the spirit ascension will our understanding of the Eternal Son become comparable to our vivid concept of the Creator Son who came to this earth [6:8.6]. And as we pass through Orvonton and Havona, the reality and nearness of the Eternal Son will continually increase [6:8.7].

Summary

The Eternal Son is the Second Source and Center of Paradise [6:1.1], and Michael is the Creator Son personalized by him and the Father, who made Nebadon and came as Jesus [7:6.3, 7:5.4]. The two are as one in nature and spirit, so that whoever has seen Michael has seen the Eternal Son [7:5.11], yet the range of their powers and functions differs [1:5.6, 7:6.4]. Now we know the Eternal Son through Michael, and as we ascend we come to know the Eternal Son more deeply [6:8.6, 6:8.7].

q159.question: How do worship and prayer differ, and how does sincere prayer reach God?
q159.answer:
The Urantia Book finds the difference between worship and prayer in their motive. "⟦Q 5:3.3⟧Worship is for its own sake⟦/Q⟧" [5:3.3]. Prayer, on the other hand, embodies a self- or creature-interest element, and that is the great difference between worship and prayer [5:3.3]. And sincere prayer is instantly conveyed over the spirit-gravity circuit of the Eternal Son to the divine personalities concerned; what is conveyed is determined not by the words but by the spiritual content they hold [7:3.3, 7:3.7].

1. What Worship Is

"⟦Q 5:3.3⟧There is absolutely no self-request or other element of personal interest in true worship⟦/Q⟧" [5:3.3]. We do not worship because of anything we may derive from God; we worship as a natural and spontaneous reaction to the recognition of the Father's matchless personality and because of his lovable nature and adorable attributes [5:3.3]. In the highest sense we worship only the Universal Father, and even when we worship the Father as he is manifested in the Creator Son, it is the Universal Father who receives the worship [5:3.1]. Worship is conveyed to the Creator through the Father's personality circuit, and the Adjusters also have authority to register the genuine adoration of their subjects in the presence of the Father [5:3.2].

2. Four Levels Within Worship

Sincere worship is the mobilization of all the powers of the human personality under the dominance of the evolving soul and subject to the directionization of the Adjuster [5:3.7]. The worship experience consists in the attempt of the Adjuster to communicate to the Father the inexpressible longings of the human soul; the mind consents, the soul craves and initiates, and the Adjuster conducts that worship [5:3.8]. True worship thus becomes an experience realized on the intellectual, morontial, spiritual, and personal levels [5:3.8].

3. The Place of Prayer

The moment an element of self-interest enters worship, devotion is transformed into prayer, and such prayer would more appropriately be directed to the Eternal Son or the Creator Son [5:3.4]. That does not mean prayer should not be offered to the Father as a part of true worship [5:3.4]. Because in the practical affairs of daily life we co-operate with the agencies of the Infinite Spirit, The Urantia Book sums it up this way: we worship God, "⟦Q 5:3.5⟧pray to, and commune with, the Son⟦/Q⟧" [5:3.5], and work out the details of our earthly sojourn with the intelligences of the Infinite Spirit [5:3.5].

4. The Way Prayer Is Conveyed

The spirit-gravity circuit is the basic channel for conveying the genuine prayers of the believing human from the level of human consciousness to the actual consciousness of Deity [7:3.3]. That which represents true spiritual value in a petition is seized by this circuit and instantly passed on to all the divine personalities concerned, each of whom takes what belongs to his domain [7:3.3]. It therefore makes no difference whether in praying one envisions the Creator Son or the Eternal Son [7:3.3]. Once something laden with supreme spiritual value arises in our consciousness and is once expressed, there is no power in the universe that can prevent its being conveyed to the absolute Spirit Personality [7:3.5].

5. Prayers That Are Not Conveyed

Conversely, purely material and self-centered petitions have no place in the spirit circuit of the Eternal Son and cannot ascend along the circuit of genuine spiritual values [7:3.6]. "⟦Q 7:3.7⟧C’est la pensée motivante, le contenu spirituel, qui valide la supplique d’un mortel.⟦/Q⟧" [7:3.7]. Words are valueless [7:3.7]. The best gift man can offer to God is the loving dedication of his will to doing the Father's will, and that constitutes the substance of true worship [1:1.2].

Summary

Worship is a loving response offered to God for what he is, asking nothing, while prayer is communion that carries our needs and wishes [5:3.3, 5:3.4]. Worship is directed to the Father, and prayer is chiefly offered to the Son [5:3.1, 5:3.5]. Sincere prayer is conveyed instantly over the spirit-gravity circuit, but what determines it is not the words but the spiritual motive [7:3.3, 7:3.7].

q160.question: What is the "spirit gravity" of the Eternal Son, and how does it draw the human soul to Paradise?
q160.answer:
Spirit gravity is the pull that acts on spiritual things, just as gravity acts on matter. The pure and universal spirit gravity of all creation leads directly back to the Second Source and Center on Paradise, the Eternal Son, and through it the Eternal Son exercises absolute spiritual sovereignty [7:1.1]. "⟦Q 7:1.1⟧Le contrôle de la gravité spirituelle universelle est la souveraineté spirituelle universelle.⟦/Q⟧" [7:1.1]. And this pull constitutes the inherent secret of the Paradise ascension of surviving human souls [7:3.2].

1. A Gravity That Responds to Quality

Just as the organized energy of physical matter, its quantity, responds to physical gravity, so spirit essence, its quality, responds to spirit gravity [7:1.3]. Spirit realities respond in accordance with their qualitative value and the actual degree of their spirit nature, and spirit gravity is always true to the qualitative spiritual status of an individual or a world [7:1.4]. Whenever spiritual reality is actualized, spirit gravity is instantly readjusted [7:1.4]. All pure spirit and all spiritual beings and values respond to the infinite drawing power of the Paradise Son [6:4.1].

2. A Force Beyond Time and Space

The gravity control of spiritual things operates independently of time and space; spirit energy is not diminished in transmission, nor does it suffer attenuation in proportion to the square of the distance [7:1.2]. Like material gravity, the spiritual gravity of the Eternal Son is absolute; sin and rebellion may interfere with the operation of the local universe circuits, but they cannot suspend spirit gravity [7:1.7]. The spiritual isolation of Urantia resulting from the Lucifer rebellion did not affect the presence and function of the spirit of the Eternal Son or of the spirit-gravity circuit [7:1.7]. The reactions of this circuit are predictable and dependable [7:1.8].

3. The Force That Draws the Soul to Paradise

The mortal mind starts out as a material mechanism, but throughout the whole ascension career it becomes progressively less subject to material gravity and more responsive to the inward pulling urge of spirit gravity [7:3.2]. "⟦Q 7:3.2⟧Le circuit de gravité d’esprit tire littéralement l’âme des hommes vers le Paradis.⟦/Q⟧" [7:3.2]. The spirit of the Eternal Son does not indwell us but encircles us, and the more the indwelling fragment of the Father attunes our mind to divine attitudes, the more responsive that mind becomes to spirit gravity [6:4.6]. The spirit fragment of the Father within and the spirit presence of the Son without work together as one for our spiritual progress [6:5.7].

4. Spiritual Attraction Between People

Spirit gravity operates not only on the universe as a whole but also between individuals and groups [7:1.6]. There is a direct attractiveness of a spirit nature between spiritually minded persons of like tastes and longings. "⟦Q 7:1.6⟧L’expression esprits apparentés n’est pas entièrement une figure de rhétorique.⟦/Q⟧" [7:1.6]. The deep sense of bond felt in a community of faith has this kind of spiritual reality.

5. Four Gravity Circuits

All gravity is circuited in the Isle of Paradise, all mind in the Conjoint Actor, all spirit in the Eternal Son, and all personality in the personal presence of the Universal Father [5:6.11]. Just as the Father draws all personalities and the Son all spiritual reality, so the Conjoint Actor exerts a drawing power over all mind [9:6.2]. The spiritual aspect of the human mind unfailingly responds to the spirit gravity of the Eternal Son, and its material aspect responds to material gravity [9:6.5].

Summary

Spirit gravity is the spiritual pull centered in the Eternal Son; it responds according to qualitative spiritual values and is not weakened by time, space, or rebellion [7:1.1-1.4, 7:1.7]. This pull literally draws the soul of man toward Paradise [7:3.2], and the more we co-operate with the leading of the Adjuster, the more responsive we become to it [6:4.6].

q161.question: What does it mean that "God is love, the Son is mercy, the Spirit is ministry"?
q161.answer:
This is a concise summary found in Paper 8: "⟦Q 8:4.2⟧God is love, the Son is mercy, the Spirit is ministry⟦/Q⟧" [8:4.2]. It does not mean that the natures of the three differ from one another; it means that one divine love is expressed in three stages. Love originates in the Father, appears as the action of mercy in the Son, and comes through the Spirit to each creature as concrete care.

1. Love: The Father

"God is love"; therefore his only personal attitude towards the affairs of the universe is always a reaction of divine affection [2:5.1]. Since the origin of all good is in the Father, the Infinite Spirit cannot possess more goodness than the Father [8:2.7]. The love of the Father is the real and eternal source of all mercy and ministry [6:3.4].

2. Mercy: The Son

The Son is the revelation of divine love to the universes; as God is love, so the Son is mercy [6:3.1]. "⟦Q 6:3.5⟧La miséricorde est l’amour appliqué, l’amour du Père en action dans la personne de son Fils Éternel.⟦/Q⟧" [6:3.5]. The Son cannot love more than the Father, but since he is himself a son of the Father, he can show mercy in an additional way, by sharing in the experience of sonship of all other sons [6:3.1]. With the proviso that the illustration is crude, The Urantia Book explains that the love of the Father is more comparable to the love of a father, while the love of the Son is more like the affection of a mother [6:3.5].

3. Ministry: The Spirit

The Infinite Spirit shares all the perfection, righteousness, and love of the Father, yet he inclines towards the mercy attributes of the Son; as the divine Sons reveal the love of God, the divine Spirit portrays the mercy of God [8:2.6]. Everlasting ministry to mind is the essence of the divine character of the Infinite Spirit, and all his offspring share the desire to minister, the divine urge to serve [8:4.1]. "⟦Q 8:4.2⟧L’Esprit est amour appliqué à la création des créatures, l’amour conjugué du Père et du Fils.⟦/Q⟧" [8:4.2]. The Spirit also ministers universal mercy in his own name and right [8:4.7].

4. Co-operation in the Three Plans

These three appear just as clearly in the plans for bringing creatures to perfection. The Father established the plan of progressive attainment, which gives the Thought Adjusters and personality [7:4.4]; the Son proposed the bestowal plan, sending the Sons of God to the evolutionary worlds to incarnate the Father's love and the Son's mercy [7:4.5]; and the Infinite Spirit, alone and of himself, devised the plan of mercy ministry, which makes the other two plans actually effective [7:4.6]. God the Father loves men, God the Son serves men, and God the Spirit inspires us to the adventure of finding the Father [3:6.8].

5. Love That Comes to Our Side

The Infinite Spirit does not take on mortal flesh as the Sons do, but he gladly undergoes a series of attenuations of divinity until he appears at last as the angels who stand by our side and guide us through the lowly paths of earth [8:4.5]. The spirit personalities of the family of the Infinite Spirit are forever dedicated to the service of the ministry of the love of God and the mercy of the Son, and "⟦Q 9:8.25⟧Ces êtres spirituels constituent l’échelle vivante par laquelle l’homme mortel s’élève du chaos jusqu’à la gloire.⟦/Q⟧" [9:8.25]. Even when the universe is forged by the hammer of suffering, those who wield the hammer are the children of mercy [9:1.8].

Summary

The Father is the source of love, the Son is mercy, that love put into action, and the Spirit is ministry, applying that love and mercy to creatures [8:4.2, 6:3.5]. The three co-operate as one in the plans of attainment, bestowal, and mercy ministry [7:4.4-4.6], and the angelic care and spiritual guidance we receive every day are, in the end, the way the Father's love reaches us [8:4.5, 9:8.25].

q162.question: If the human mind comes from the Infinite Spirit, can our minds be called divine?
q162.answer:
The answer of The Urantia Book is that the source is divine, but our minds as they are now are not yet divine. The realms of creature mind are of exclusive origin in the Third Source and Center, and he is the bestower of mind [9:5.2], but that does not mean we should presume all phenomena of mind to be divine. "⟦Q 9:5.5⟧Le Créateur Conjoint est la source du mental, mais le mental n’est pas le Créateur Conjoint.⟦/Q⟧" [9:5.5].

1. Where Mind Comes From

The Third Source and Center is absolute only in the domain of mind; the bestowal of mind upon the seven superuniverses is derived from the Seven Master Spirits, and our local universe is pervaded by the Nebadon modification of the Orvonton type of cosmic mind [9:4.3]. The human mind is an individualized circuit, an impersonal part, of the cosmic mind bestowed upon the local universe by the Creative Daughter of the Third Source [9:5.4]. The Infinite Spirit ministers to human and subhuman intellects through the adjutant spirits of the local universe [9:5.3]. Mind of the human order is the bestowal of the daughters of the Conjoint Actor, the divine ministers of the evolving universes [3:1.8]. Even if the universe were to grow infinitely, his mind potential would be sufficient to endow an unlimited number of creatures with mind [9:5.1].

2. What Mind Does

"⟦Q 9:4.5⟧L’énergie est chose, le mental est signification, l’esprit est valeur.⟦/Q⟧" [9:4.5]. Mind transmutes the values of spirit into the meanings of intellect, volition brings those meanings to fruit in the material and spiritual worlds, and personality unifies these factors [9:4.6]. The ministry of mind is also the groundwork for the indwelling of the Adjuster. "⟦Q 9:5.2⟧Même les fragments du Père trouvent impossible d’habiter le mental des hommes avant que le chemin n’ait été convenablement préparé pour eux par l’action mentale et la fonction spirituelle de l’Esprit Infini.⟦/Q⟧" [9:5.2].

3. Why, Then, It Is Not Yet Divine

Human intellect is rooted in the material origin of the animal races [9:5.5]. Just as physical nature is no true revelation of the beauty of Paradise, so universe intelligence is no true revelation of God who is mind [9:5.5]. Mind on Urantia is a compromise between the essence of thought perfection and immature human nature [9:5.6]. "⟦Q 9:5.6⟧Le mental a vraiment une origine divine et surement une destinée divine, mais votre mental humain n’est pas encore de dignité divine.⟦/Q⟧" [9:5.6].

4. What Defiles the Mind

The Urantia Book points out that all too often we sully our minds with insincerity and sear them with unrighteousness, subject them to animal fear, and distort them with useless anxiety [9:5.7]. Therefore mind as we know it is hardly worthy of great admiration, much less of worship, and the contemplation of immature human intellect should lead to humility [9:5.7]. Mind that is subservient to matter becomes increasingly material, but mind that yields itself to spirit becomes increasingly spiritual and attains survival and eternity [1:3.7].

5. The Way Mind Reaches Its Divine Destiny

The Infinite Spirit is personally conscious of every mind, and every true intellectual value, divine thought, and perfect idea is unerringly drawn into his absolute mind circuit [9:6.1, 9:6.2]. Mind gravity can operate independently of material gravity and spirit gravity, but wherever those two operate, it always functions together with them [9:6.3]. Because the Infinite Spirit is the absolute source of our mortal minds, we sometimes grasp the reality of the Spirit more easily than that of the Son [6:8.5]. The Infinite Spirit is the perfect expression of the Creator's mind toward all creatures, and the Supreme Being is the evolving expression of all creatures' minds toward their Creator [9:6.9].

Summary

The human mind has a divine origin, coming from the Infinite Spirit by way of the adjutant spirits and the cosmic mind [9:5.2, 9:5.4], but because of its animal roots and its immaturity it has not yet attained divine dignity [9:5.5, 9:5.6]. Mind is the instrument that deals with meaning [9:4.5], and when it yields itself to spirit it grows toward its divine destiny [1:3.7].

q163.question: What does it mean that justice is not a personal attitude of the Father, the Son, or the Spirit but a function of the Trinity?
q163.answer:
The Urantia Book does not regard justice as the feeling or disposition of any single divine person. "⟦Q 10:6.2⟧La justice n’est jamais une attitude personnelle, elle est toujours une fonction plurale.⟦/Q⟧" [10:6.2]. Goodness, mercy, and truth are the universe ministry of the divine personalities, but justice is the Trinity attitude that these personalities of love, mercy, and ministry form together [10:6.2]. That is why no one of the Paradise Deities alone fosters the administration of justice [10:6.2].

1. The Division of Labor Between Law and Justice

"⟦Q 10:6.1⟧Toute loi prend origine dans la Source-Centre Première ; elle est la loi.⟦/Q⟧" [10:6.1]. The administration of spiritual law inheres in the Second Source and Center, the revelation and interpretation of law is the function of the Third Source and Center, and the application of law, justice, falls within the province of the Paradise Trinity and is carried out by certain Sons of the Trinity [10:6.1]. The evidence on which fairness rests is supplied by the personalities of the Infinite Spirit [10:6.3], and judgment, the final application of justice in accordance with that evidence, is carried out by the Stationary Sons of the Trinity [10:6.4].

2. The Trinity Is an Association of Persons

The Trinity is not an individual. "⟦Q 10:4.3⟧La Trinité est une association de personnes infinies fonctionnant impersonnellement, mais sans contrevenir à la personnalité.⟦/Q⟧" [10:4.3]. Calling the illustration crude, The Urantia Book compares it to a father, son, and grandson forming a corporate entity subject to their personal wills [10:4.3]. The Father, Son, and Spirit can co-operate as individuals as they wish, but that is not in itself the Trinity [10:4.4]. The function of the Trinity is not simply the sum of the attributes of the three Deities but a union that gives rise to new meanings, values, and powers [10:5.2]. It is therefore more fitting to speak of the Trinity as having functions rather than attributes, such as the administration of justice, totality attitudes, co-ordinate action, and cosmic overcontrol [10:5.1].

3. The Sons of the Trinity Who Administer Justice

The Stationary Sons who carry out this justice include the Trinitized Secrets of Supremacy, the various orders of the Ancients of Days, the Perfectors of Wisdom, the Divine Counselors, and the Universal Censors [10:6.5-6.15]. They represent the collective attitude of the Trinity only in the domain of executive judgment, that is, of justice [10:6.16]. The Ancients of Days and their associates mete out fair judgment throughout the seven superuniverses, while in the central universe such functions exist only in theory, since fairness is self-evident in perfection [10:6.17]. The decree of extinction for sin-identified beings also comes from the tribunals of the superuniverse [2:3.3].

4. The Relation Between Justice and Mercy

"⟦Q 10:6.18⟧Justice is the collective thought of righteousness; mercy is its personal expression⟦/Q⟧" [10:6.18]. Mercy is the attitude of love, and precision characterizes the operation of law [10:6.18]. Divine judgment is the soul of fairness, ever conforming to the justice of the Trinity while ever fulfilling the love of God, and when fully understood, the righteous justice of the Trinity and the merciful love of the Universal Father are coincident [10:6.18].

5. What It Means for Us

This teaching keeps us from misunderstanding God the Father as a cold judge. In his personal relations the Father is always a loving Father [4:4.6], and justice is a plural function arising from the three persons together taking the whole into account. The Trinity is concerned only with the total: the whole planet, universe, superuniverse, and grand universe [10:7.2]. So as individuals we can rely on the Father's love, and as regards the order of the universe as a whole we can trust the fair justice of the Trinity.

Summary

Law comes from the Father, the Son administers spiritual law, and the Spirit reveals law, but justice, the application of law, is the function of the Trinity [10:6.1]. Justice is not a personal attitude but a plural function [10:6.2], carried out by the Stationary Sons of the Trinity according to the evidence presented by the personalities of the Infinite Spirit [10:6.3, 10:6.4]. Justice is the collective thought and mercy the personal expression, and when fully understood the two coincide [10:6.18].

q164.question: What is the "self-distribution" of the Universal Father, and in what ways does the Father work in the universe today?
q164.answer:
Self-distribution refers to the policy by which the Universal Father, from the eternal past, has given away to his Sons and creatures everything that he could detach from himself and share [10:1.1]. The Father has reserved to himself only that which he finds it impossible to delegate or bestow [10:1.1], and everything else he has actually bestowed, together with the dignity of personality possession [10:1.2]. As a result, the Father works in the universe today not directly and alone but in seven ways, through the Son, the Spirit, Paradise, and his own fragments [10:3.9-3.16].

1. Why He Gives Himself Away

"⟦Q 10:1.3⟧Divine personality is not self-centered⟦/Q⟧" [10:1.3]. Self-distribution and sharing of personality characterize divine freewill selfhood; just as creatures crave association with other personalities, so Creators are moved to share divinity with their children [10:1.3]. Even after bestowing himself so lavishly, the Father has not in the least diminished his possession of power, wisdom, and love [3:4.1].

2. Giving Himself to the Son and the Spirit

The Father bestows the personality of infinity upon his only-begotten Son, and the two together bestow the conjoint personality of their eternal union upon the Infinite Spirit [10:1.4]. The Father thereby ceased to exist as an unqualified personality, and so we must depend on the revelation of the Eternal Son in order to know the Father [10:1.4]. This is not a loss but a liberation. The Trinity delivers the Father from personality absolutism [10:0.1], and by this way the Father possesses unlimited capacity to become the divine father of every will creature [10:2.1]. "⟦Q 10:3.5⟧Fatherhood is not real without sonship⟦/Q⟧" [10:3.5].

3. Seven Ways in Which the Father Works

In the universes outside Havona the Father functions as Creator through the Creator Sons, as Controller through the gravity center of Paradise, as spirit through the Eternal Son, and as mind through the Conjoint Creator [10:3.10-3.13]. As a Father he maintains parental contact with all creatures through his personality circuit [10:3.14], and as a person he acts directly through his fragments, which in mortal man are the Thought Adjusters [10:3.15]. And as total Deity he functions only in the Paradise Trinity [10:3.16].

4. Self-Chosen Limitations

"⟦Q 10:3.17⟧Tous ces abandons et délégations de juridiction par le Père Universel sont entièrement volontaires et imposés à lui-même par lui-même.⟦/Q⟧" [10:3.17]. In the affairs of a local universe the Father has made each Creator Son as perfect and authoritative as the Eternal Son [10:1.2]. Because of his infinity God cannot communicate directly with lowly creatures, so in love he steps down and attenuates his infinity through the incarnation of his Sons, the personalities of the Infinite Spirit, and the Adjusters [2:1.7, 2:1.8]. Yet he has reserved to himself the prerogative of bestowing personality and the privilege of direct contact through the personality circuit [5:0.2].

5. What It Means for Us

Because of the Father's self-distribution, we do not merely gaze vaguely at a distant God; we relate directly to the Father through the Adjuster within us and the personality circuit that encompasses us [10:3.14, 10:3.15]. At the same time, to know the Father we must look for trustworthy information in the bestowals of the Sons he has sent, especially in the life of Michael, who came to this earth [10:1.6].

Summary

Self-distribution is the loving policy by which the Father has freely given away everything he could share to the Son, the Spirit, and his creatures [10:1.1, 10:1.2, 10:1.3]. As a result the Father works in seven ways, through the Creator Sons, Paradise, the Eternal Son, the Conjoint Creator, the personality circuit, the Adjusters, and the Trinity [10:3.9-3.16], and all these limitations are self-chosen [10:3.17].
